title: Human Flourishing in the Age of AI @ SF
description:
AI is transforming how we work, create, think, and live. The possibilities are extraordinary. Yet even those closest to the technology are increasingly questioning what these changes mean for our identity, purpose, agency, and what makes life worth living.

What if AI could help humans not just do more, but become more?

About the Roundtable

We’re bringing together individuals deeply engaged with AI, each offering a distinctive perspective shaped by their expertise, firsthand experience, and independent thinking.

We want to connect perspectives that rarely meet — from people building AI systems, to those studying the human mind, exploring new forms of creative expression, or examining AI’s broader impact on society.

Format

A two-hour roundtable combining small-group discussions and collective reflection, followed by optional informal conversations.

We’re not here to force consensus or rush into solutions. We want to challenge assumptions, uncover blind spots, and find questions worth pursuing pursuing together.

title: Command Line Music - Auwen Workshop
description:
This class is an intro to command line music with Auwen, a tool for writing and performing songs in real time using a command line interface.

You'll get hands-on experience building tracks from scratch and playing them in a low stakes, collaborative setting. No prior coding or music experience needed.

What to expect: installation takes about 5 minutes. Your first beat, maybe an hour. Playing a full set takes a 3-6 weeks of practice depending on experience level.

A few students have gone on to perform live sets at SF events and festivals as part of Soniare Collective. With just a bit of dedication you could be next! We would love to have you join our growing family of music producers.

After the class you'll be invited to our Discord where we do multiplayer jam sessions, so there's space to keep learning and playing with other people.

Workshop Outline

• Software and sample installation
• Overview of Auwen User Interface and workflow
• Multiplayer learning session creating genres you suggest
• Solo time creating music on your own computer
• Wrap-up and share resources for further learning

Educational Goals

To inspire participants and offer an accessible entry point into performing live dance music, while building foundational skills in livecoding, composition, improvisation, and real-time musical decision-making.

Instructor

Nes Croft is a musician, artist, and computer engineer from Montana who has written and recorded thousands of songs since a young age starting with folk/rock as a teenager and expanding into experimental pop, IDM, techno, and trance. Nes gained an interest in electronics at age 19 after working at the DIY synth company Synthrotek in Portland, OR. Going on to earn a bachelor's degree in computer engineering at Montana State University. While in college Nes co-founded and developed Vaytricks Beat Machine, a mobile drum machine app that received over 100,000 downloads. 5 years later Nes left Vaytricks to pursue a live performance focused approach to music production and Auwen was born. Auwen is a digital audio workstation featuring a hybrid producer/DJ workflow that allows musicians to perform dance music live using a command line interface. Given the nature of the software, Nes naturally gravitated toward live music events testing Auwen at various electronic music festivals in Montana. Later, Nes joined the livecoding scene in San Francisco and started hosting workshops & live music events at TIAT art gallery and Gray Area in San Francisco in 2025-2026.

Preparation

Bring a laptop/headphones and install the software auwen.app to save time in class. Also bring water and maybe a light snack to keep your energy up because we'll be covering a lot of information! Some drinks may be provided as well. When you arrive come through the front of TIAT then all the way back and down the stairs on the left. The event is in the TIAT basement.

🎉 Public Hours at the Commons 🎉

Every Sunday, the Commons opens to the public — no membership required. Come co-work, connect, create, or just explore the space at your own pace. ✨

🕘 When: Every Sunday, 9 AM – 10 PM

Public Hours are self-guided — come in, settle in, and make the space your own. Weekends are usually unstaffed, so there's no check-in desk or guided tour. Your entry code comes by email. Once you RSVP, we'll send you a personal QR code — that's your key for the day. Keep it handy on your phone (and check spam if you don't see it).

Your access stays active all day, 9 AM – 10 PM, so you can come and go freely.

Can't find your code on the day? No problem — scan the QR posted on the door to check in and get a fresh one on the spot.

We're shoes-off 🧦 — please clean up after yourself, including dirty dishes and mugs, and use only the front entrance. Trouble getting in? Email hello@thesfcommons.com.

title: Bryce 3D Live: make art with 30 year old software | co-presented by Culture Slop
description:
Inspired by the VFX collective Corridor Crew’s video “Can modern VFX Artists use 90’s software?”, we’re hosting a Bryce 3D Live event here in San Francisco.

10 artists with different practices will be making live worlds and scenes with Bryce 7.1 on a collection of 15-year-old working iMac G5s donated to TIAT from the Internet Archive. There will also be a version available in an online emulator for you to try it yourself on your own laptop. + We’ll have a surprise panel to vote on the coolest images.

Bryce (named after Bryce Canyon, Utah) is 3D modeling software first released by MetaTools in 1994 released until 2010. If you’ve ever seen Trapper-Keeper-core graphics of floating islands with mirrored spheres, some rusty pipes with tendrils in a devastated world (but there's also a chess piece), or a glowing orb on a cover of an ambient music CD from 2002 you found in a thrift store, that was probably made with Bryce!

Its skeuomorphic interface (designed by Kai Krause) has alien-like buttons and is confusing as hell to play with, but that’s why it’s fun. During the peak of digital art webrings from 1998-2002 hobbyists across the world built scenes and shared them in online galleries. (And people are still doing this today on r/Bryce3D!) I’ll kick off the event with some Bryce / Metascape lore and images I dug up on the Wayback machine.

Event Schedule

2:00-2:15pm - Mingle time + artists gather around the computers

2:15pm - Intro to the Strangeness of Metascape and early Bryce Communities (a short talk)

2:30pm - Artists begin 3D modeling! You can observe them, hang out, or play with Bryce too

4:30pm - Judgement Ceremony with special guest panelists

5:00pm - Say goodbye

Artists:
Shubha Jagannatha (@shubhastudios)
Jason Eppink (@jasoneppink)

Enchax (@chaxnsee)
Isaac Gierard (@igierard) + more TBA

Emulator and streaming by Britt Selvitelle + InfiniteMac with software from Macintosh Repository

Artifacts from Susan A. Kitchens (author of Real World Bryce 4) and special guest Phil Clevenger (UX design director of KPT Bryce 1.0 & Bryce 2).

Hosted by Danielle Baskin (@djbaskin)

Bring a laptop if you want to play too! But you are very welcome to hang out and watch.

A weekly space for real conversations, meaningful connection, and a deeper sense of belonging.

🌿 About This Gathering

Maybe you've got plenty of people in your life, but still sometimes feel lonely. Maybe you find it hard to move beyond small talk and social scripts. Maybe you sometimes struggle to feel like you truly belong, even when you're surrounded by people. Or maybe you're simply curious about what makes some relationships and communities feel easy, genuine, and nourishing — while others don't.

Each week, we'll explore a different aspect of connection and belonging: loneliness, vulnerability, authenticity, being seen, boundaries, desire, conflict, and what gets in the way of feeling connected and at home with others.

This isn't a workshop where you sit and listen to someone talk about connection. We'll actually practice connecting with one another. Thanksgiving can be tender—beautiful for some, complicated for others.
This year, The Commons opens its doors as a warm landing place for anyone seeking connection, comfort, or simply a table to belong at.

Join us for A Commons Friendsgiving, a cozy day of slow crafting, shared projects, and a communal feast led by Cody’s famous, soul-warming beef stew. Throughout the day, the space will hum with gentle creativity—jewelry making, writing, painting—and the soft ebb of people arriving whenever it feels right.

At 6:30pm, we gather for dinner: a potluck-style feast shaped by whatever delicious dishes our community brings together. Afterward, we’ll melt into a shared food-coma glow with cartoons or movies on the projector, chosen collectively in the moment.

Whether you’re a member, someone’s +1, or simply a person looking for a place to land on Thanksgiving Day, you’re welcome here. This is a space for found family, gentle joy, and the quiet magic of being together.

🕰 Flow / Schedule

• All Day (Drop-In):
Crafts, personal projects, soft socializing, settling in. Come whenever resonates.
• 6:00pm – 6:30pm:
Warm mingling, arrivals, potluck setup.
• 6:30pm:
Friendsgiving Dinner — beef stew + community dishes.
• 7:30pm – 9:30pm:
Post-dinner unwind: communal crafting stations, movie/cartoon chosen together, open conversation, rest, cozy vibes.

• Please go to the front door at 540 Laguna Street (see the stairs to the basement to the left of Earthbody).
• RSVP to this Luma event (if you haven't already) and check your inbox for the email address that is associated with your Luma account for 2 emails:
One from us and one from "Kisi" with the subject "Your QR Code and link for access at The SF Commons.".

If you’d like a full plate and first pick at the potluck, plan to arrive by 6:30pm when dinner begins.

👥 Facilitators

Cody Hasty
Space Operations Manager at The Commons. Cody is on a personal mission to cultivate belonging and nurture the “found family” that lives and grows within these walls. A dedicated maker, cook, and gentle community steward, Cody crafts spaces where people can exhale deeply and feel at home.

💫 Who This Is For

• Commons members and their +1s
• Anyone who doesn’t have another place to land on Thanksgiving
• Folks craving connection, warmth, and low-pressure community time
• People aligned with The Commons’ values of care, creativity, and civic belonging
• All experience levels, all identities, all backgrounds welcome

🎒 What to Bring (Optional)

• A dish to share for the potluck feast
• Any crafts, books, or personal projects you’d like to work on
• Dietary needs? Please message Cody in advance so he can coordinate something delicious for you too

The Commons is a civic temple for wisdom, belonging, and beauty in San Francisco — a place where community, creativity, and care come alive. We host gatherings that nourish the individual and the collective, weaving a culture of curiosity, kindness, and shared stewardship.

🎉 Public Hours at the Commons 🎉

Every Sunday, the Commons opens to the public — no membership required. Come co-work, connect, create, or just explore the space at your own pace. ✨

🕘 When: Every Sunday, 9 AM – 10 PM

📍 Where: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco (corner of Hayes & Laguna, basement level)

RSVP and we'll email you your entry code ahead of time — so you can let yourself straight in when you arrive.

──────────────────────────────

🧭 A self-guided day

Public Hours are self-guided — come in, settle in, and make the space your own. Weekends are usually unstaffed, so there's no check-in desk or guided tour. Our members are glad to answer questions about the space; for anything else — including guided tours, which we don't offer as drop-ins — email hello@thesfcommons.com ahead of time.

──────────────────────────────

🔭 Getting in

Your entry code comes by email. Once you RSVP, we'll send you a personal QR code — that's your key for the day. Keep it handy on your phone (and check spam if you don't see it).

• Find us. We're at 540 Laguna St, on the corner of Hayes & Laguna. Head down the stairs beside Earthbody to the basement level — that's the Commons.
• Scan your QR code at the reader to unlock the door. Hold your phone just below the Kisi reader by the door and it'll let you in.

Your access stays active all day, 9 AM – 10 PM, so you can come and go freely.

Can't find your code on the day? No problem — scan the QR posted on the door to check in and get a fresh one on the spot.

We're shoes-off 🧦 — please clean up after yourself, including dirty dishes and mugs, and use only the front entrance. Trouble getting in? Email hello@thesfcommons.com.

Maybe you've got plenty of people in your life, but still sometimes feel lonely. Maybe you find it hard to move beyond small talk and social scripts. This isn't a workshop where you sit and listen to someone talk about connection. We'll actually practice connecting with one another. title: 🧠 The Thought Experiment Lab
description:
Note: while there are many guests listed in the RSVP, most of these are carried over from previous events in this series. We don't expect much more than 30 to attend.

"Imagination without reason is mere fancy, but reason without imagination is sterile. That is partly why scientists and philosophers alike have always used imaginary scenarios to help sharpen their ideas and push them to their limits." - The Pig that Wants to be Eaten, by Julian Baggini

For this meeting (December 2), we'll be discussing the whether we can know things by intuition and how we might know things like:

• 2 + 2 = 4
• A belief chosen at random cannot be justified
• An action is free only if you could have done otherwise
• It is wrong to cause suffering for no reason

Please review this very brief primer on the norms of philosophical discussion: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Gj3HesfWz4A2kEAMSY0x7hNxvJZNtiCexUeilJXVak8/edit?usp=sharing

• It is highly recommended to read this article: https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/intuition/

• Read sections 1.3, 2.1-2.3, and 3.1-3.5

Some examples of topics we've discussed at past meetings:

• Do you survive being teleported?
• Is God required to have morality?
• What are the limits of free speech?
• Is it moral to breed pigs that want to be eaten?
• Should crimes be punished before they happen?
• Are some pleasures more noble than others?
• Do immoral people just have bad luck?
• Is monogamy unethical?
• Is the existence of evil a problem for belief in God?
• Should we try to become immortal?
• Are we obligated to do much more to the world's poor?
• Is it okay to deliberately create a disabled child?
• Is it permissible to kill and eat animals?
• Should we enter the experience machine?
• Is science the only source of knowledge?
• Is what is right or wrong a matter of opinion?
• On what basis should we care about the environment?
• Can we know we are not brains in a vat?
• What is a potential person worth?
• What is gender?
• What is philosophy and how is it done?
• Is abortion morally permissible?
• Does philosophy make assumptions?
• Is evolutionary psychology a legitimate science?
• Should paid organ donation be permitted?
• Can we have knowledge without certainty?
• Is adult consensual incest always immoral?
• Is everything we do ultimately motivated by self-interest?
• Is it immoral to have children?
• Are there good arguments against objective morality?
• Should we use genetic therapies to increase intelligence?
• Is it morally permissible to select your child's race?
• Does free will require the ability to do otherwise?
• Do our lives have meaning?
• Can dating preferences be irrational or discriminatory?
• Is happiness the only thing that matters to one's well-being?
• Was the universe created by God?
• Is morality only about the greatest good for the greatest number?
• How important is it to preserve minority cultures?

title: Command Line Music - Auwen Workshop
description:
This class is an intro to command line music with Auwen, a tool for writing and performing songs in real time using a command line interface.

You'll get hands-on experience building tracks from scratch and playing them in a low stakes, collaborative setting. No prior coding or music experience needed.

What to expect: installation takes about 5 minutes. Your first beat, maybe an hour. Playing a full set takes a 3-6 weeks of practice depending on experience level.

A few students have gone on to perform live sets at SF events and festivals as part of Soniare Collective. With just a bit of dedication you could be next! We would love to have you join our growing family of music producers.

After the class you'll be invited to our Discord where we do multiplayer jam sessions, so there's space to keep learning and playing with other people.

Workshop Outline

• Software and sample installation
• Overview of Auwen User Interface and workflow
• Multiplayer learning session creating genres you suggest
• Solo time creating music on your own computer
• Wrap-up and share resources for further learning

Educational Goals

To inspire participants and offer an accessible entry point into performing live dance music, while building foundational skills in livecoding, composition, improvisation, and real-time musical decision-making.

Instructor

Nes Croft is a musician, artist, and computer engineer from Montana who has written and recorded thousands of songs since a young age starting with folk/rock as a teenager and expanding into experimental pop, IDM, techno, and trance. Nes gained an interest in electronics at age 19 after working at the DIY synth company Synthrotek in Portland, OR. Going on to earn a bachelor's degree in computer engineering at Montana State University. While in college Nes co-founded and developed Vaytricks Beat Machine, a mobile drum machine app that received over 100,000 downloads. 5 years later Nes left Vaytricks to pursue a live performance focused approach to music production and Auwen was born. Auwen is a digital audio workstation featuring a hybrid producer/DJ workflow that allows musicians to perform dance music live using a command line interface. Given the nature of the software, Nes naturally gravitated toward live music events testing Auwen at various electronic music festivals in Montana. Later, Nes joined the livecoding scene in San Francisco and started hosting workshops & live music events at TIAT art gallery and Gray Area in San Francisco in 2025-2026.

Preparation

Bring a laptop/headphones and install the software auwen.app to save time in class. Also bring water and maybe a light snack to keep your energy up because we'll be covering a lot of information! Some drinks may be provided as well. When you arrive come through the front of TIAT then all the way back and down the stairs on the left. The event is in the TIAT basement.

title: Command Line Music - Auwen Workshop
description:
This class is an intro to command line music with Auwen, a tool for writing and performing songs in real time using a command line interface.

You'll get hands-on experience building tracks from scratch and playing them in a low stakes, collaborative setting. No prior coding or music experience needed.

What to expect: installation takes about 5 minutes. Your first beat, maybe an hour. Playing a full set takes a 3-6 weeks of practice depending on experience level.

A few students have gone on to perform live sets at SF events and festivals as part of Soniare Collective. With just a bit of dedication you could be next! We would love to have you join our growing family of music producers.

After the class you'll be invited to our Discord where we do multiplayer jam sessions, so there's space to keep learning and playing with other people.

Workshop Outline

• Software and sample installation
• Overview of Auwen User Interface and workflow
• Multiplayer learning session creating genres you suggest
• Solo time creating music on your own computer
• Wrap-up and share resources for further learning

Educational Goals

To inspire participants and offer an accessible entry point into performing live dance music, while building foundational skills in livecoding, composition, improvisation, and real-time musical decision-making.

Instructor

Nes Croft is a musician, artist, and computer engineer from Montana who has written and recorded thousands of songs since a young age starting with folk/rock as a teenager and expanding into experimental pop, IDM, techno, and trance. Nes gained an interest in electronics at age 19 after working at the DIY synth company Synthrotek in Portland, OR. Going on to earn a bachelor's degree in computer engineering at Montana State University. While in college Nes co-founded and developed Vaytricks Beat Machine, a mobile drum machine app that received over 100,000 downloads. 5 years later Nes left Vaytricks to pursue a live performance focused approach to music production and Auwen was born. Auwen is a digital audio workstation featuring a hybrid producer/DJ workflow that allows musicians to perform dance music live using a command line interface. Given the nature of the software, Nes naturally gravitated toward live music events testing Auwen at various electronic music festivals in Montana. Later, Nes joined the livecoding scene in San Francisco and started hosting workshops & live music events at TIAT art gallery and Gray Area in San Francisco in 2025-2026.

Preparation

Bring a laptop/headphones and install the software auwen.app to save time in class. Also bring water and maybe a light snack to keep your energy up because we'll be covering a lot of information! Some drinks may be provided as well. When you arrive come through the front of TIAT then all the way back and down the stairs on the left. The event is in the TIAT basement.
